title: Gap-Protected Heisenberg-Limited Squeezing with Locally Interacting Multi-Level Spins
authors: Sakshi Bahamnia, Sagar Chaudhary, Arman Duha, Thomas Bilitewski
abstract: We demonstrate a general mechanism to generate scalable, metrologically useful entanglement in the form of generalized spin squeezing in multi-level (qudit) spin systems with power-law interactions. We demonstrate this for spin-changing dynamics, extending the physics of spin-nematic squeezing known from spinor BECs to spatially extended lattice geometries. In the absence of all-to-all connectivity, the dynamics generally suffers from leakage into non-collective finite-momentum modes, destroying Heisenberg scaling. We show that introducing local $\mathfrak{su}(D)$ exchange interactions establishes an energy gap that protects the fully symmetric collective manifold, suppressing non-collective excitations, and achieving Heisenberg scaling $ξ^2\propto1/N$ in one to three dimensions for any power-law exponent. We provide an analytical understanding of the mechanism via the analysis of the Bogoliubov excitation spectrum, and demonstrate its effectiveness via numerical simulations of the quantum many-body dynamics. Our findings more broadly apply to other spin-squeezing Hamiltonians, and directly generalize to larger internal spin dimensions. Our results provide a practical pathway towards scalable Heisenberg-limited qudit entanglement generation in experimental platforms such as arrays of (polar) molecules, magnetic atoms, and Rydberg atoms realizing multi-level spin systems.
summary: This work develops a general mechanism to achieve Heisenberg-limited spin squeezing in multi-level spin systems with local interactions. By introducing a specific local exchange interaction, the authors create an energy gap that suppresses detrimental non-collective excitations. This restores optimal entanglement scaling, offering a practical pathway for quantum sensing using arrays of multi-level atoms or molecules.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of generating scalable, metrologically useful entanglement (spin squeezing) in multi-level spin systems when interactions are short-ranged.
main_result: Introducing a local $\mathfrak{su}(D)$ exchange interaction establishes an energy gap that protects the collective manifold, thereby restoring Heisenberg scaling ($\xi^2 \propto 1/N$) for any power-law interaction range.
method: The analysis combines analytical techniques, such as Bogoliubov theory applied to the excitation spectrum, with numerical simulations using the generalized discrete truncated Wigner approximation (GDTWA).
model_or_system: The system is a $d$-dimensional array of $N$ multi-level (qudit) spins with power-law interactions, modeled by a Hamiltonian that includes a gap-protection term.
key_observables:
Spin squeezing parameter ($\xi^2_{	ext{opt}}$), Heisenberg scaling exponent ($

important_parameters: Interaction exponent ($\alpha$), spatial dimension ($d$), system size ($N$), and the gap-protection strength ($\chi$).
main_assumptions: The Bogoliubov analysis is assumed valid when excitation density is low; the GDTWA is an approximation method.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition from non-scalable to Heisenberg-limited squeezing as gap protection is added, show time evolution of squeezing, and map out phase diagrams based on interaction range and disorder.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of squeezing loss with local interactions, then introduces the gap-protection mechanism, analyzes the scaling laws analytically via Bogoliubov theory, and finally validates these findings through extensive numerical simulations across various dimensions and disorder levels.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, tunable mechanism (the gap-protection term) to overcome fundamental limitations (loss of scaling due to locality) in generating high-quality entanglement in platforms like Rydberg or molecular arrays.

(a) Power-law interacting spin-1 particles undergo pair creation |0, 0⟩→|+1, −1⟩, which generates entanglement; the local su(3) exchange Vij ˆλi · ˆλj protects the collective dynamics. (b) Hilbert-space sectors la- beled by SU(3) irreducible representations (p, q) and separated by gaps of the quadratic Casimir ˆΛ · ˆΛ. In the collective sec- tor (N, 0), states are labeled by occupations |N−1, N0, N+1⟩; arrows indicate the states coupled by pair creation.

FIG. 2. Phases of squeezing dynamics without gap protection (χ = 0). (a) Minimal squeezing ξ2 min (color scale) as a function of dimension d and power-law exponent α, showing the collec- tive regime (blue, ξ2 opt ∼1/N) and the non-collective regime (ξ2 min ∼N −ν, ν < 1), for L1D = 104, L2D = 100, L3D = 22. (b) Time evolution of ξ2 opt in 3D for a characteristic α in the collective regime (blue, α = 1.5) and in the non-collective regime (red, α = 5.0), for L3D = 5, 7, 10, 15, 22 from faint to dark. (c) Extracted scaling exponent ν of ξ2 min ∝N −ν versus α for 1D, 2D and 3D (error bars smaller than symbol size).

FIG. 4. Robustness to site-dilution disorder. (a) Minimal squeezing ξ2 min as a function of site dilution p and gap pro- tection strength χ in 3D for L = 10 (N = 1000) for dipolar interactions (α = 3). (b) Minimal squeezing Nξ2 min versus gap protection strength χ for different p (colorbar). Inset: Scaling collapse of minimal squeezing.

FIG. 3. Gap-protected squeezing phase diagrams. (a-c) Mini- mal squeezing as a function of α and gap protection strength χ in 1D (L = 1000) (a), 2D (L = 32) (b) and 3D (L = 10) (c). (d) Scaling of minimal squeezing versus system size N for parameters below and above the transition with markers as indicated in the panels (a)-(c). (e) Scaling exponent of minimal squeezing ξ2 min ∝N −ν versus gap protection strength χ normalised by the Bogoliubov prediction χc,bog. The collec- tive phase is defined by ν reaching 1.
